Power forward | nickname = | class = Freshman | career_start = 2007 | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 11 | weight_lb = 220 | nationality = USA | birth_date = {{birth date and age|1989|7|15}} | birth_place = [[Wurzbach, Germany]] | highschool = [[Woodrow Wilson High School (Dallas, Texas)|Woodrow Wilson High School]][http://www.nbadraft.net/admincp/profiles/anthonyrandolph.html NBADraft.net profile][http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Anthony-Randolph-1069/ DraftExpress profile] | awards = }} '''Anthony Randolph''' (born [[July 15]], [[1989]] in [[Wurzbach, Germany]]) is a [[college basketball]] power forward for [[Louisiana State University|LSU]].[http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/player/profile?playerId=36181 ESPN.com profile] He is considered a top prospect for the [[2008 NBA Draft]]. ==Early days== Anthony Randolph went to school in Pasadena and Little Rock before coming to Woodrow Wilson High School as a junior.[http://www.lsusports.net/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=27829&SPID=2166&DB_OEM_ID=5200&ATCLID=945722&Q_SEASON=2007 LSUsports.net profile] Playing for Pat Washington at Woodrow Wilson, he averaged 25.8 points per game and 12.6 rebounds as a senior. He was named to the first team All-Area Dallas Morning News boys basketball team and had 21 points in the 2007 Roundball Classic in Chicago. ==College== Randolph made an impact on the court right away, as he had six blocks in just the third game of his freshman season.[http://www.lsusports.net/downloads1/28518.htm?ATCLID=1311022&SPSID=27828&SPID=2166&DB_OEM_ID=5200 Box Score from Southeastern Louisiana vs. LSU] He was the only LSU Tiger to start all 31 games.
